description: Provenance-locked application evidence and explicit Styrene P0 mobile workflow decisions

references.name: Sideband

notes: The APK manifest identifies io.unsigned.sideband version 2.1.0 build 20251128, minimum API 24, target API 33, and arm64-v8a native libraries.
The APK contains RNS 1.5.2 and LXMF 1.1.1 version constants, but not their exact revisions.
The public 2.1.0 tag points to 1402bb6a492e87dc5224139a300cbb547487f7b6 and contains stale 1.9.2 application metadata.
A signed release manifest names private origin c98a6eb43e8946d8283c3d05865064542e95787e, which is not publicly resolvable.
The release APK was re-uploaded; the SHA-256, not the release name alone, identifies the inspected artifact.

limitations: No retained executed Android workflow exists.
No current iOS artifact exists.
Source-to-APK reproducibility and exact bundled RNS and LXMF revisions are unresolved.
Sideband is not protocol authority or interoperability evidence.

references.name: Reticulum MeshChat

notes: Annotated tag v2.4.0 has tag object 303f3dbd8163f3bfa31ab3a30844d3aceae7678b and peels to the recorded revision.

Requirements declare rns>=1.3.7 and lxmf>=1.0.1; exact Android runtime versions require an executed app-info capture.
The v2.4.0 release contains desktop assets only and provides no iOS installation path.

limitations: No retained executed Android workflow exists.
Android OS, Termux, Python, RNS, LXMF, browser, and built frontend versions are unknown.
The PWA manifest is not iOS RNS or LXMF execution evidence.
Reticulum MeshChat is not protocol authority or interoperability evidence.

facts: The application persists one primary identity and exposes identity display, export, and import controls.
Android connectivity settings persist outbound TCP host, port, IFAC name, and passphrase and require a service or application restart to apply.
Canonical delivery and propagation announces populate actionable peer and propagation-node lists.
SQLite persists conversations and terminal messages; no durable draft store was found and startup removes outbound and sending rows.
The composer clears after local router handoff and database ingestion, not proven recipient delivery.
Message presentation distinguishes preparing, waiting for path, establishing link, sending, delivered, propagated, failed, cancelled, and rejected.
Manual retry deletes the failed record and creates a new message.
Propagation-node selection is independent and persisted; manual sync exposes progress, cancellation, completion, duplicates, and typed terminal failures.
Loss of the Reticulum and LXMF service is disclosed as lost connectivity requiring restart.
limitations: Static inspection is not an executed UI or network observation.
No Android device, OS, correlation, accessibility tree, screenshot, recording, or runtime log was retained.
Displayed delivery states cannot independently establish authenticated receipt semantics.
No Sideband evidence can satisfy protocol interoperability or packaged Styrene gates.

facts: The Android procedure runs the Python backend in Termux and opens the Vue frontend in a separate browser.
Identity, configuration, announces, messages, read state, and propagation selection are file or SQLite backed.
TCP client host and port are configurable, but interface changes require a full MeshChat restart and status is only connected or disconnected.
Canonical delivery announces are persisted by destination hash and projected into the peer list.
Composer text is component-local and clears after HTTP send acceptance; no durable draft or draft revision guard was found.
Message presentation distinguishes generating, outbound, sending, sent, delivered, rejected, cancelled, and failed.
Manual retry deletes the old message before creating a replacement; failed messages may also retry automatically after an announce.
Startup converts outbound, sending, and opportunistic-sent messages to failed rather than resuming them.
Propagation selection, manual synchronization, cancellation, completion count, periodic synchronization, and detailed terminal errors are exposed.
The v2.4.0 rejected state is omitted from one terminal progress loop; post-release commit df5aea94eab7f4be1cdfef494446e9d6979aed77 fixes it.
limitations: Static inspection is not an executed UI or network observation.
No Android device, OS, Termux, Python, browser, app-info response, correlation, or runtime artifact was retained.
Dependency lower bounds do not identify exact installed RNS or LXMF versions.
No Reticulum MeshChat evidence can satisfy protocol interoperability or packaged Styrene gates.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Cold launch creates or restores one stable identity and exposes its public delivery identity without implying a route.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Both packaged targets show the same restored public identity and explicit custody status from backend state.
proposed_differences: Styrene requires explicit custody state and fail-closed production storage rather than inferring safety from persistence.
exclusions: Private key export is not required by the mobile minimum.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: The operator configures and persists one validated TCP client endpoint independently of RNode and propagation settings.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: The current backend generation reports connecting, connected, reconnecting, degraded, or failed with a typed reason.
proposed_differences: Styrene applies validated configuration through a typed session instead of requiring an unexplained process restart.
exclusions: TCP server administration is not part of the mobile minimum.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Canonical lxmf.delivery announces upsert peers by destination hash with name, aspect, source, and freshness.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: People lists each destination once and distinguishes discovery from route, link, or online state.
proposed_differences: Styrene preserves typed announce provenance and never labels discovery as connectivity.
exclusions: Noncanonical announce aspects cannot establish a messaging peer.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Durable canonical messages form conversations with stable ordering, unread state, and contact identity.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Inbound content appears once, unread changes are durable, and empty live state contains no preview records.
proposed_differences: Styrene requires a typed start-conversation path from canonical discovery.
exclusions: Attachments and group conversations are outside the mobile minimum.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Each conversation draft is durable and revisioned, and send completion clears only the accepted revision.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Failure preserves editable text and a late result cannot erase a newer edit.
proposed_differences: Styrene intentionally requires stronger draft persistence and revision safety than either static candidate implementation shows.
exclusions: Cloud draft synchronization is not required.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: An explicit Direct request persists one canonical outbound message before dispatch and returns its identity.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Two packaged peers exchange one message and reply with exact source, destination, content, and correlation.
proposed_differences: Styrene clears the draft only after backend acceptance rather than frontend HTTP or router handoff alone.
exclusions: Local acceptance is not recipient delivery.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Persistence, transport acceptance, propagation upload, and authenticated recipient delivery remain separate evidence.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Message details expose the exact terminal backend evidence and never promote queued, sent, or propagated to delivered.
proposed_differences: Candidate Delivered labels remain comparison inputs until executed LXMF evidence establishes their semantics.
exclusions: A screenshot or displayed label cannot prove a receipt.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Retry retains the canonical message identity and creates or resumes a correlated backend attempt without duplicate delivery.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: The same message shows another attempt and an authoritative retryable or terminal outcome.
proposed_differences: Styrene intentionally does not copy Sideband and MeshChat behavior that deletes the failed record and creates a replacement.
exclusions: Automatic retry policy is a separate product decision.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Identity, endpoint, conversations, messages, unread state, contacts, drafts, propagation selection, and attempt truth survive restart.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Graceful restart and forced process death restore committed state once and disclose incomplete work explicitly.
proposed_differences: Styrene preserves canonical attempt history instead of deleting or silently replacing in-flight records during startup.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: A separately persisted, currently compatible propagation selection gates upload and bounded manual or automatic synchronization.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: The application distinguishes selection readiness, upload, retrieval progress, durable-before-ack storage, duplicates, and terminal failure.
proposed_differences: Styrene validates current announce and policy metadata before enabling propagated composition.
Styrene automatic synchronization is tied to bounded connection and foreground opportunities rather than an unqualified interval.
exclusions: Propagation hosting, peering, capacity, and expiry administration are outside the mobile product.

parity_rows.styrene_requirement: Stopped, starting, connecting, connected, reconnecting, degraded, and failed states are generation-scoped and include typed recovery reasons.
parity_rows.observable_styrene_outcome: Endpoint refusal, path loss, unavailable propagation, partial boot failure, and stale completion remain distinct and recoverable where applicable.
proposed_differences: Styrene intentionally exposes a finer typed session model than connected or disconnected labels and restart instructions.
exclusions: Animated activity cannot substitute for backend state.
